reasons: The action accurately preserves the stated condition for a new business with only two customers and the recommendation to use the reviews/testimonials already available.

It also correctly retains the longer-term recommendation to increase review volume by sending people links to review destinations. The source does not set a numeric volume target or platform priority, which the candidate appropriately leaves unresolved.
The action and conditional wording are supported: the source asks recipients who found the delivered review useful to consider reviewing it on the currently promoted review site.

The prerequisite is imprecise and partly circular: delivery of the review is the event in which the request is made, not a prerequisite that must already have been completed. It also reverses the source framing, in which the recipient requested the review from Exposure Ninja. Revise the prerequisite to state that the recipient has requested the review, or omit it and retain the delivery-email trigger.
This is correctly presented as a counseling-business example rather than a universal instruction.
The candidate accurately captures the source’s suggested timing (as clients leave) and prompt for obtaining feedback about a free initial consultation.
The warning is supported by the source’s explicit criticism of placing the call to action at the bottom of the page and its characterization of that approach as a really bad idea.
The candidate does not invent an exception or a measurable placement threshold absent from the excerpt.
The quoted instruction supports putting a prominent box at the top right and making the intended action obvious.

The surrounding layout discussion expressly describes the right-hand box as an Amazon desktop-page convention. The candidate presents top-right placement as unqualified despite the excerpt not providing a mobile-layout recommendation. Scope the action to the discussed desktop layout or make the primary requirement that the conversion goal be highly visible.
The source expressly calls a comment about a free consultation a great testimonial for the page advertising that offer.
The action accurately conveys the intended use: show evidence that other people considered and benefited from requesting the same consultation or offer.
The two phone-number placements and clickability of the top-page number are accurately taken from the client-site example.

The source describes these elements as part of one example and a broader approach, but does not state that adding phone numbers depends on first implementing candidate 6d017428f5eb06987430e399f6b46c2e1642333080f556f8119556b279433355. The declared depends_on relation imposes an unsupported dependency and should be removed or recast as contextual association.
The source does say, in the speaker’s approach, to take Amazon’s form because it works well and has educated users how to buy.

The candidate broadens this into a categorical instruction to avoid novel interaction patterns. The excerpt discusses agencies creating unique solutions, but ends before completing the statement about when not to be a pioneer, so that contrast is not fully established by the supplied passage.

The depends_on relation to the Amazon-layout example is also not an explicit implementation prerequisite in the source. Remove the unsupported dependency and limit the action to adopting the Amazon form/conventions described.
The claim is directly supported by the source’s statement that user-testing videos can make users appear unintelligent regardless of the product or audience.

Its title appropriately preserves the source’s important framing that this appearance occurs when people are unfamiliar with the site and are busy or distracted; it does not claim that users actually lack intelligence.

source_limitations: The excerpt ends mid-sentence after “If you're going to be the first person to”, so the source’s intended qualification about when not to be a pioneer is incomplete.
The excerpt provides no numerical review-volume target, method for determining review credibility, or prioritization among the named review destinations.
The layout guidance is principally illustrated through desktop Amazon and a client-site example; it does not specify a mobile layout or responsive-design treatment.
Claims such as Amazon having a good conversion rate are asserted by the speaker without supporting evidence or measurement details in this excerpt.
